Twenty-four templates, each one Typst file that compiles to a six-slide square deck, 21 by 21 centimetres, the canvas LinkedIn and Bluesky show without cropping.

There is no package to install and nothing to import.
Copy the file, replace the project block at the top, and rewrite the slides.
The templates share a vocabulary so that moving between them is easy, and they share nothing else, so a copy of one is complete on its own.

All of them announce the same fictional release.
The words are held constant on purpose: the only thing that changes from one template to the next is the design.

Start with [using a template](get-started.qmd), or open any deck below and read its source.

## Editorial

Paper, a serif, and a single column.
For an announcement that is an argument rather than a feature list.

::: {#gallery-editorial}
:::

## Terminal

Shell chrome and monospace as the leading voice.
For something used from a command line.

::: {#gallery-terminal}
:::

## Technical

Grids, rules, and measurement marks.
For engineering work that should read as a specification.

::: {#gallery-technical}
:::

## Data visualisation

A chart carries the slide, drawn from Typst primitives rather than a plotting package.
For a release with a number that moved.

::: {#gallery-dataviz}
:::

## Panels

Content divided into cards or ruled rows.
For a walkthrough, or a set of parallel points.

::: {#gallery-panels}
:::

## Control

A user interface metaphor: switches, crosshairs, a stepped ladder.
For a release that turns something on, or replaces a manual step.

::: {#gallery-control}
:::

## Poster

Display type and one large motif.
For short copy that can carry a slide on its own.

::: {#gallery-poster}
:::

## Screenshot

Framed product shots as the evidence.
For an announcement about what the output looks like.

::: {#gallery-screenshot}
:::
